title: Pull Request Quality Gates knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Pull Request Quality Gates?
options: Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Required status checks and branch rules prevent a merge until the intended validation has passed; reviewers should verify expected checks cannot be skipped.
questions.answer_key: Required status checks and branch rules prevent a merge until the intended validation has passed; reviewers should verify expected checks cannot be skipped.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of pull request quality gates: Required status checks and branch rules prevent a merge until the intended validation has passed; reviewers should verify expected checks cannot be skipped. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Required status checks”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.

Make the check deterministic and fail with a meaningful status when requirements are not met. Preserve reports where useful and configure required branch checks to match the checks the workflow actually emits.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: Make the check deterministic and fail with a meaningful status when requirements are not met. Preserve reports where useful and configure required branch checks to match the checks the workflow actually emits.
questions.explanation: Required status checks: Make the check deterministic and fail with a meaningful status when requirements are not met. Preserve reports where useful and configure required branch checks to match the checks the workflow actually emits. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to pull request quality gates?
options: Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Required status checks and branch rules prevent a merge until the intended validation has passed; reviewers should verify expected checks cannot be skipped. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
